instruction: I am going on a vacation. Move my go-to-sleep phone alarm to 1 hour later and disable the rest.
notes: Single app (phone). The phone username is the supervisor's phone number, so phone-login is gated on (profile-known) from supervisor.show_profile as well as (passwords-known). phone.update_alarm is modeled as ONE action (name matches the API) carrying alarm_id, access_token and the two optional arguments the task uses (time, enabled); the values it must pass are given per alarm by the static facts desired-time / desired-enabled, which are derived from phone.show_alarms at runtime: the alarm labelled 'Go to sleep' keeps enabled=true and gets its listed time + 1 hour, every other enabled alarm gets enabled=false and its own current time (passing the unchanged time leaves that field untouched in the database, so only `enabled` changes for those alarms). Each alarm is updated at most once ((not (alarm-updated ?al)) precondition), so the resulting alarm-time / alarm-enabled facts are exactly the final state; no fact is ever both added and deleted by one action. The number of non-target alarms is only known at runtime; the problem instantiates two placeholder enabled alarms (alarm-other-1/2) and should be re-instantiated with one object per enabled non-target alarm returned by show_alarms (already-disabled alarms must not be touched). supervisor-complete-task takes the alarm records as non-API parameters; its precondition (all three alarms updated as required, target being the go-to-sleep alarm) is equivalent to the goal conjunction given the static desired-* facts, and it is forced to be the last action because every other action requires (not (task-completed)).
